set.title: Parallelize the aufsicht quality pipeline
set.body:
## Destination

Decide whether and how to parallelize the aufsicht quality pipeline (`quality-fast` and `quality-full`), covering both inter-gate scheduling and intra-gate pytest parallelism, targeting Blacksmith's 4-core runners. Preserve report determinism and existing gate-failure semantics. The one deliberate semantic change in scope: redesign the `ToolingError`-abort contract so gates already running when another gate raises finish instead of being killed, and all tooling errors from the run are collected rather than surfacing only the first. Implementation is a separate, later effort — this map produces a decision and design, not the code.

## Notes

- Runner code: `src/aufsicht/pipeline.py` (`GATE_ORDER`, `run_pipeline`), `src/aufsicht/adapters/*`, `src/aufsicht/report.py` (`Report.tooling_error`), `src/aufsicht/ratchet.py` (`base_worktree`).
- Constraints already established: the integrity gate always runs first (v5.1 §11.3); a normal gate *failure* already doesn't abort the loop today — only a `ToolingError` does; no gate currently reads another gate's `GateResult`, so gates are independent by data flow.
- Environment: Blacksmith-hosted runners, 4 cores, fixed for now — concurrency degree decisions should target this ceiling.
- Two separate optimization levers, tracked as separate tickets: inter-gate scheduling (running independent gates concurrently) and intra-gate parallelism (pytest, which alone accounts for ~3 of the ~4 minute `quality-full` run).
- Known hazard already found: `base_worktree()` in `ratchet.py` does an unlocked check-then-`git worktree add`; several adapters (pyright, pyscn, xenon, deptry) call it and also mutate the shared `ctx.report` — a race under concurrent execution.
- Skills to consult per ticket: `grilling` and `domain-modeling` by default; `research` for AFK investigation tickets.

## Decisions so far

## Not yet specified

- How a parallel gate design affects CI log/progress UX (streaming subprocess output from concurrent gates) — revisit once the execution-model ticket resolves.
- Whether a "fail fast" opt-out should remain available for local dev iteration even after the default becomes "let others finish" — revisit once the tooling-error-collection ticket resolves.
- How pytest-xdist's worker count and gate-level concurrency degree share the 4-core budget if both land — revisit once both the execution-model and pytest-parallelism tickets resolve.
- Whether the ToolingError-abort semantic change requires updating the pinned v5.1 guardrails spec or is purely an internal runner behavior — revisit once the tooling-error-collection ticket resolves.

## Out of scope

set.title: Audit shared mutable state across gate adapters for concurrency hazards
set.body:
## Question

Which parts of the gate adapters and shared runner state (`ctx.cache`, `base_worktree()`, `project_env()`, ratchet-cache files, `ctx.report` mutation) are unsafe to touch from more than one gate concurrently, and what would each need (locking, per-worker cache keys, read-only sharing) to be made safe? Produce a findings list: one hazard per adapter/shared resource, with a recommended fix shape (not an implementation) for each.

Known starting hazard: `base_worktree()` in `src/aufsicht/ratchet.py` does an unlocked check-then-`git worktree add`, and `pyright`, `pyscn`, `xenon`, and `deptry` adapters all call it and also write into `ctx.report.exemption_reasons` / `ctx.report.metrics`.

set.title: Decide the inter-gate concurrency execution model
set.body:
## Question

How should independent gates in `GATE_ORDER` actually be scheduled concurrently: thread pool, process pool, or asyncio subprocess management (each gate already just shells out via `subprocess.run`, so this is I/O-bound, not CPU-bound, in Python)? What's the worker count / concurrency degree given the 4-core Blacksmith ceiling — and should it be configurable via `.quality/config.toml`? How does "integrity always runs first" (v5.1 §11.3) and the pre-computed ratchet exemptions (`compute_exemptions`, which must finish before any gate runs) fit around the parallel dispatch of the rest of `GATE_ORDER`?

set.title: Redesign the ToolingError contract to collect concurrent gate errors
set.body:
## Question

Today `Report.tooling_error` is a single field and any `ToolingError` aborts the remaining gate loop (`src/aufsicht/pipeline.py`). Once gates run concurrently, a `ToolingError` from one gate should let already-running gates finish rather than being killed, and the report should collect every tooling error from the run. Decide: the schema shape (e.g. an additive `tooling_errors: list[ToolingError]` with `tooling_error` kept as a backward-compatible alias for the first one), the `status`/`exit_code` semantics when a run mixes passes, fails, and tooling errors from concurrently-completed gates, and whether this changes anything the pinned v5.1 guardrails spec or distribution spec documents about the tooling-error contract.

set.title: Investigate pytest-xdist feasibility for aufsicht's own test suite
set.body:
## Question

`pytest` alone accounts for roughly 3 of the ~4 minutes `quality-full` takes today. Would running aufsicht's own test suite under `pytest-xdist` (`-n auto` or a fixed worker count fitting the 4-core Blacksmith ceiling) be safe and worthwhile? Investigate: whether tests rely on shared global/session state, fixed temp paths, or the git worktrees the suite creates against generated scratch repos (per `AGENTS.md`'s "self-test suite ... executing the v5.1 §18 and distribution §8 tables against generated scratch repositories") in ways that would collide across xdist workers; whether any tests are order-dependent; and an estimate of the wall-clock benefit at 4 cores. This is independent of the inter-gate scheduling tickets — it's about parallelism *inside* the pytest gate alone.

text: Findings: docs/research/concurrency-hazard-audit.md on branch research/concurrency-hazard-audit (commit ad6af46). Four hazards found: (1) unlocked check-then-git-worktree-add race in base_worktree() (ratchet.py L95-119), shared by ruff/pyright/pyscn/xenon/deptry ratchet paths; (2) pyscn scratch-dir collision between cycles and deadcode gates sharing the repo cwd; (3) unsynchronized mutation of Report.metrics/exemption_reasons from adapter code; (4, low severity) ratchet cache-file races, self-healing via atomic rename. project_env()/analyzer_env() already lock-protected, no changes needed. Recommended fixes: SHA-keyed file lock around base_worktree(), and move all Report mutation out of gate workers into a post-gather merge step in the orchestrator.

Findings: docs/research/pytest-xdist-feasibility.md on branch research/pytest-xdist-feasibility (commit 56b5879). Verdict: likely safe to adopt with no test-code changes. The ~3-minute cost is aufsicht's own tests/ suite (227 tests, measured via --collect-only), not the pytest_adapter gate. Nearly all tests use per-test tmp_path scratch repos (xdist-safe); the one shared resource (TEST_CACHE analyzer-env cache in conftest.py) is already lock-protected by toolchain.py's advisory file lock. pytest-xdist is not yet a dependency (one-line addition). Recommend starting with a fixed -n 4 matching the Blacksmith ceiling over -n auto. Wall-clock benefit not empirically measured this pass (would require actually adding the dependency and timing a run).

reason: Four hazards documented with fix shapes in docs/research/concurrency-hazard-audit.md (research/concurrency-hazard-audit branch); env-build path already safe.
Likely safe with no test-code changes; findings in docs/research/pytest-xdist-feasibility.md (research/pytest-xdist-feasibility branch).

set.title: Implement pipeline parallelization
set.body: Implementation follow-on to the decisions made on the wayfinder map [Parallelize the aufsicht quality pipeline](AUFSI-xndjcp) (closed). See that map's Decisions so far for full rationale and the linked research findings.

set.title: Lock base_worktree()'s check-then-create race
set.body: Wrap the check-and-create in base_worktree() (src/aufsicht/ratchet.py) in a SHA-keyed file lock, mirroring the advisory-lock pattern toolchain.py already uses for env builds. Prerequisite for running ratcheted gates (ruff, pyright, pyscn deadcode, xenon, deptry) concurrently. See docs/research/concurrency-hazard-audit.md (Hazard 1).

set.title: Fix pyscn scratch-directory collision between cycles and deadcode gates
set.body: Give each pyscn invocation (src/aufsicht/adapters/pyscn.py) its own isolated output directory instead of sharing <repo>/.pyscn/, so the cycles and deadcode gates are safe to run concurrently. See docs/research/concurrency-hazard-audit.md (Hazard 2).

set.title: Move Report mutation out of gate workers into a post-gather merge
set.body: Gate functions currently mutate ctx.report (metrics, exemption_reasons, gates.append) directly. Change gate functions to return their GateResult plus any metric/reason payload; have the orchestrator merge into Report only after every worker in the concurrent pool has completed, so field population order stays deterministic regardless of finish order. See docs/research/concurrency-hazard-audit.md (Hazard 3).

set.title: Build the concurrent gate scheduler
set.body: Refactor run_pipeline (src/aufsicht/pipeline.py): run integrity, then compute_exemptions synchronously, then dispatch the rest of GATE_ORDER as one flat ThreadPoolExecutor pool (no priority ordering). Default 4 workers, configurable via a new [gates] max_workers key in .quality/config.toml (src/aufsicht/config.py). Submit all gates up front and let the whole pool drain to completion regardless of any ToolingError. Decision: AUFSI-xpa61s on the closed map.

set.title: Adopt pytest-xdist for aufsicht's own test suite
set.body: Add pytest-xdist to the dev dependency group (pyproject.toml) and wire a fixed -n 4 into the CI step that runs tests/ (.github/workflows/aufsicht.yml). No test-code changes expected. Decision: AUFSI-1x2syq on the closed map, findings in docs/research/pytest-xdist-feasibility.md.

set.title: Cut the aufsicht CI wall clock (M1-M3)
set.body:
## Destination

Merge the three milestones of CI-SPEED-PLAN.md: one shared, persisted CI cache; the self-test suite as a parallel CI job under xdist; and a fast gate-side pytest (pinned pytest-xdist plus per-gate durations). End state: Blacksmith ~7 -> ~2-2.5 min, GitHub Actions 12-15 -> ~4-5 min, with BOTH suite executions kept (pinned-env gate run and ambient-interpreter step run).

## Notes

- This map carries execution (override of the plan-don't-do default): tickets are PR-sized implementation tasks, each landing as its own PR.
- Standing context: CI-SPEED-PLAN.md at the repository root of this branch. Every number there was measured on 2026-08-24; the xdist safety claim is proven by experiment (-n 4 green, identical counts, 2.60x). Read the relevant section before starting any ticket.
- PR classes: changes to src/aufsicht or tests/ are normal PRs. Changes to .github/workflows/** or .quality/** are guardrail PRs on protected paths: own approved PR, human review (v5.1 section 11.2/11.3, deployment model B). An agent drafts; a human approves.
- Decided before charting: cancel-in-progress applies to pull requests only (a main push is never cancelled mid-publish); the per-gate duration field is a report schema change, so a MAJOR version bump per distribution spec section 10 (0.1.0 -> 0.2.0, all five places); Milestone 4 work and the t80xhw gate-parallelization epic stay outside this map.
- The known cost structure, for orientation: the pytest gate is 96 percent of quality-full (397.7 s of 414.3 s measured); all 12 other gates plus the env build are 16.6 s; the suite runs twice per CI run; the job splits its cache over three roots and persists nothing.

## Decisions so far

## Not yet specified

- Whether $RUNNER_TEMP resolves to a byte-stable path across runs on Blacksmith and GitHub-hosted runners (restored venv shebangs depend on it; an unstable path silently costs the cache win through self-healing rebuilds). Verify from the first M1 CI run.
- The vCPU count of the GitHub-hosted runners this repository actually uses (2 vs 4): decides whether -n 4 oversubscribes there. Decide after M1 lands, from the first GHA run timings.

## Out of scope

- Milestone 4 of CI-SPEED-PLAN.md: pip-audit result cache with TTL, consumer-template caching, parallel gate execution inside run_pipeline, ruff invocation dedup, deterministic commit dates with ratchet-cache reuse. Gate parallelization is tracked by the t80xhw epic, untouched by this map.
- Directions rejected with data in CI-SPEED-PLAN.md section 5: porting the runner to another language, reducing fetch-depth, deleting one of the two suite executions.

set.title: Rework aufsicht.yml: one cache root, actions/cache, parallel selftests job, concurrency, timeout
set.body:
## Question

Milestone 1 of CI-SPEED-PLAN.md, as one guardrail PR on the protected path .github/workflows/aufsicht.yml (own approved PR, human review per v5.1 section 11.2/11.3):

1. Job-level env for both jobs: AUFSICHT_CACHE_DIR and AUFSICHT_TEST_CACHE = \${{ runner.temp }}/aufsicht-cache (one literal, stable path). tests/conftest.py:26-27,61 respects both, so the gate, in-process test calls, and scratch CLI children then share one root. Today the job uses three roots and builds the 434 MB analyzer env up to three times per run.
2. An actions/cache step before the installs: path = the cache dir from (1); key = aufsicht-v1-\${{ hashFiles('.quality/toolchain.lock', 'tests/fixtures/scratch.py', 'pyproject.toml') }}; restore-keys = aufsicht-v1- (keeps base worktrees and ratchet counts warm across lock bumps; env dirs are content-keyed, so stale subdirectories are harmless). Blacksmith accelerates actions/cache with no change.
3. Move the self-test suite into its own job selftests that runs in parallel with quality-full: checkout, setup-python 3.12, install ". uv pytest pytest-xdist", then "python -m pytest tests -q -n 4" with the same job-level cache env. Note: pip does not read the [dependency-groups] dev group, so pytest-xdist must be on this install line.
4. Add selftests to the publish job's needs, so a self-test failure still blocks publishing (today it blocks transitively through the quality-full job).
5. Add concurrency: group \${{ github.workflow }}-\${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress \${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }} (decided: PRs only; a main push is never cancelled mid-publish). Add timeout-minutes: 30 to both jobs.
6. Optional: setup-python cache: pip with cache-dependency-path: pyproject.toml. Keep fetch-depth: 0 (measured 1-3 s; the gate exits 3 without it).

Acceptance: same report artifact shape; second CI run shows a cache hit; pass counts unchanged (202 passed, 25 skipped in both suite executions). Estimated effect: Blacksmith ~7 -> ~4 min, GHA 12-15 -> ~6-7 min.

set.title: Add a session prewarm fixture for the scratch analyzer env
set.body:
## Question

Milestone 2.1 of CI-SPEED-PLAN.md, normal PR in tests/. Add a session-scoped autouse fixture in tests/conftest.py that calls aufsicht.toolchain.analyzer_env on the scratch lock (and the default project env) before the first test. Under pytest-xdist each worker triggers it; the existing O_EXCL advisory lock (src/aufsicht/toolchain.py:206-266) serializes the build while the other workers poll. This removes the multi-minute env build from inside the first test and stops worker build races. Tolerate a worker dying mid-build (stale-lock takeover after 1800 s already exists). A network failure then surfaces as a session-scoped error rather than a per-test one; that is accepted.

set.title: Make the scratch toolchain lock byte-identical to the repo lock
set.body:
## Question

Milestone 2.2 of CI-SPEED-PLAN.md, normal PR in tests/. tests/fixtures/scratch.py:25-41 renders SCRATCH_TOOLCHAIN without the three leading comment lines of .quality/toolchain.lock, so the analyzer-env key (sha256 of lock bytes, src/aufsicht/toolchain.py:296) differs and one shared cache root still yields two 434 MB envs. Add the same three comment lines so the bytes match. Verified safe: test_audit_fixes.py:85-91 and the other lock assertions only do substring/prefix checks (test_selftests.py:71-75, test_ratchet_selftests.py:129,151). Effect: one analyzer env everywhere, ~430 MB less cache, one less cold build.

set.title: Runner: optional pytest-xdist pin support plus [tests] runner_args passthrough (inert)
set.body:
## Question

Milestone 3, runner half (PR R of CI-SPEED-PLAN.md section 4), normal PR in src/aufsicht, landed INERT until the guardrail PR flips it on:

a. project_env_pins (src/aufsicht/toolchain.py:334-345) accepts an optional pytest-xdist entry in the lock and installs it into the project env when present.
b. The pytest adapter (src/aufsicht/adapters/pytest_adapter.py:161-176) passes the [tests] runner_args (hook already defined at src/aufsicht/config.py:132) to the pinned pytest. Default stays sequential when no pin and no args exist.
c. Self-tests for both behaviors, including the default-off path (no pin, no args, command unchanged).

set.title: Runner: per-gate durations in the report plus MAJOR version bump
set.body:
## Question

Milestone 3c of CI-SPEED-PLAN.md, normal PR in src/aufsicht. Add a wall-clock duration per gate: fill a duration extra on each GateResult from the pipeline loop (src/aufsicht/pipeline.py:142-171); GateResult.to_dict merges extras (src/aufsicht/model.py:107-112) and no existing extra key is named duration (verified), and no test asserts an exhaustive report key set (verified). This makes every later win and regression visible in the uploaded aufsicht-report.json.

Version class: a report schema change is MAJOR per distribution spec section 10 (spec/aufsicht-distribution-spec-v1.md line 397). Bump 0.1.0 -> 0.2.0 in all five places (pyproject.toml, src/aufsicht/__init__.py, install/bootstrap.sh, skill/scripts/bootstrap.sh, .quality/toolchain.lock) in the same commit, per the repository release convention. The toolchain.lock line is part of that sanctioned release act.

set.title: Runner: verify restored analyzer-env versions against the lock
set.body:
## Question

Milestone 3d of CI-SPEED-PLAN.md, normal PR in src/aufsicht, meaningful once CI caches the env dir (blocked by the workflow ticket). _env_complete (src/aufsicht/toolchain.py:176-203) trusts a .aufsicht-ok marker plus entry-point shebang checks and never compares installed versions with the lock, so a marker-present but wrongly-restored cache runs wrong tool versions. On a marker-valid hit, read the installed version from dist-info for each pinned tool and compare with toolchain.lock; on mismatch, rebuild. No subprocess --version calls needed. A failed verification is a rebuild, never a pass.

set.title: Guardrail PR: pin pytest-xdist in toolchain.lock and set [tests] runner_args
set.body:
## Question

Milestone 3, guardrail half (PR G of CI-SPEED-PLAN.md section 4). One approved PR on the protected paths, only after the inert runner support has landed:

1. .quality/toolchain.lock: add pytest-xdist = "<exact version>" (exact pin, never a range, per v5.1 section 4.4). The project env then contains it (wired by the runner ticket).
2. .quality/config.toml [tests]: runner_args = ["-n", "4"]. Fixed 4, not auto: the Blacksmith 4-vCPU ceiling is the target and auto oversubscribes smaller machines.

Acceptance: the gate's pytest run inside "aufsicht full" finishes ~2.6x faster with identical outcomes (202 passed, 25 skipped), the report artifact keeps its shape, and exit codes 0/1/2/3 are unchanged (test_spine.py, test_selftests.py cover them).

text: origin/claude/blacksmith-ci-performance-419uh3 (commit 2749697, based on ca1ea69, merges cleanly into main) already implements items 1-4 and 6 of this ticket: job-level AUFSICHT_CACHE_DIR + AUFSICHT_TEST_CACHE at /home/runner/.cache/aufsicht (the default root, one shared cache), actions/cache@v4 over envs/projenvs plus the uv/pip/pyscn/pip-audit download caches keyed on hashFiles(toolchain.lock, uv.lock, pyproject.toml) with restore-keys, a parallel self-test job running pytest tests -q -n auto with pytest-xdist on its install line, and publish.needs = [quality-full, self-test]. Its Blacksmith measurements corroborate the plan: gate pytest 4m37s of 4m44s, analyzers ~6s, xdist 3.4x on 4 cores. Still missing from this ticket: item 5 (concurrency group with PR-only cancel-in-progress, timeout-minutes: 30), and the step uses -n auto where this map decided fixed worker counts (Blacksmith 4 vCPU; auto oversubscribes smaller GHA runners). Keep this ticket open until those land; the branch can serve as the PR base.

PR #4 (https://github.com/code-factorio/aufsicht/pull/4, branch ci-speed/m1-workflow) implements this ticket in full: 2749697 rebased onto main (the original branch claude/blacksmith-ci-performance-419uh3 was left untouched on origin after a force-push guard correctly refused to rewrite it) plus one commit adding the concurrency guard with PR-only cancel-in-progress, timeout-minutes: 30 on both jobs, and -n 4 per the map's fixed-worker-count decision. Awaiting reviewer merge — the protected-path approval act. Acceptance after merge: second run shows an actions/cache hit; 202 passed, 25 skipped in both suite executions.

PR #4's red run has two causes. (1) integrity gate fails BY DESIGN: .github/workflows/aufsicht.yml is a protected path and the tripwire fires on any PR that changes it, not overridable by the allowlist — merging the reviewed PR is the approval act (deployment model B), and the post-merge main run sees an empty diff and passes. (2) pytest gate + self-test job fail on two tests/test_spine.py base-resolution tests: GitHub sets GITHUB_BASE_REF on every pull_request event, run_cli blanks it for scratch subprocesses but not for in-process resolve_base calls — pre-existing, every pull_request run in repo history is red. Fixed by PR #5 (ci-speed/fix-ci-env-leak, autouse no_ci_base_env fixture; red reproduced and full suite green under leak simulation). Sequence: merge #5 first, then rebase #4 onto main so its pytest gate goes green; #4 then merges with only the designed integrity tripwire red.

reason: Merged to main via PR #4 (9543e88 + 33a4eae) after PR #5 fixed the pre-existing CI-env leak that had failed every pull_request run. Workflow now: quality-full and self-test as parallel jobs, one shared persisted cache root (/home/runner/.cache/aufsicht via job-level AUFSICHT_CACHE_DIR + AUFSICHT_TEST_CACHE), actions/cache over envs/projenvs/uv/pip/pyscn/pip-audit keyed on hashFiles(toolchain.lock, uv.lock, pyproject.toml), self-test with pytest-xdist -n 4, publish needs both jobs, concurrency group with PR-only cancel-in-progress, timeout-minutes 30. The red integrity tripwire on the PR was the designed deployment-model-B approval act; post-merge main runs pass it. Acceptance to confirm from the next runs: cache hit from the second run on, both suite executions green.
